handoff: No blocking findings. All six conditions, the JSON state and exit codes 0/7/2/3 are covered by tests; unit tier, typecheck and story-wait.test.ts are green. Nits: an unrequested --interval flag; a stop signal exits 7 like a timeout.

findings.title: --interval was not in the issue
findings.detail:
The issue's Wanted line is `norn story wait <story> --until <condition> [--timeout <d>] [--json]`. The change also adds `--interval <d>` (default 5s). It is small, documented and harmless, but it is extra surface nobody asked for.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Keep it, or drop it and keep the 5s poll internal. Either way, say so in the PR body.

findings.title: A stop signal exits as a timeout (7)
findings.detail:
SIGINT ends the wait with ExitCode.timeout, so a supervisor cannot tell 'I was stopped' from 'time ran out'. This is documented in the header comment and tested, so it is a deliberate choice. It does weaken the 'exit codes tell endings apart' goal a little.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Optional: leave as is, or exit 130 on a signal as main.ts does on a second signal.
